_comment: How arrangement_status_service.py applies Suzanne Chhour's rule of 13 Oct 2026 for
accounts whose RCS status is an instalment / promise-to-pay / dishonour status
(in_scope_statuses) but that have no active arrangement behind it. Runs after the
status and treatment step mappings and overrides their derived columns:
active instalment = a row in RC_ARRANGEMENT for the debt with a next instalment date;
active deal       = a row in RC_DEAL for the debt (payment in full / part payment /
settlement) with a due date - past due dates included (Suz 13 Oct:
a PTP stays active through Debtrak's grace period; carry any PTP
with a due date over, exceptions are few and managed by hand);
an in-scope open account with neither:
- on a mapped RCS treatment (Treatment_NewTreatmentCode set by the step rule):
status -> with_treatment_code.status, step unchanged;
- no treatment, debt age <= without_treatment_code.max_age_days:
status -> young.status, step -> young.step;
- no treatment, older: status -> old.status, no treatment (step cleared).
Accounts with an active instalment or deal keep the status account_status_codes.json
gave them. Closed accounts (closed_date set) and statuses outside the scope are not
touched. RC_ACCOUNT_EXTRACT.Arrangement_Active records what the rule saw for each
in-scope open account: INSTALMENT, DEAL or NONE (NULL outside the scope).
Scope and definitions confirmed by Suz in the Treatment Mapping chat, 13 Oct 2026:
INSTAL: 'there is a payment plan recorded on account with a next instalment date';
PTP: 'there is an active payment in full (or part pay, or settlement) on account
with a due date'. Everything else keeps the agreed status mapping.
